events.title: 6th Wikidata Workshop
events.organizers: Nicolas Ferranti, Marcelo de Oliveira Costa Machado, Jorão Gomes Jr., Simon Razniewski, Axel Polleres, Markus Kroetzsch and Peter Patel-Schneider
events.description:
Wikidata is an open knowledge base hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation
that can be read and edited by both humans and machines. As the central
repository for structured data used by Wikipedia, Wiktionary,
Wikisource, and many other Wikimedia projects, Wikidata has become an
essential resource for academic research and industrial applications,
supporting data integration, semantic technologies, and knowledge-driven
systems.

Over the years, a growing body of research and practical innovation has
highlighted Wikidata's role as a cornerstone of open structured
knowledge. Previous editions of the Wikidata Workshop have addressed
topics such as data quality, multilingual knowledge contributions,
community dynamics, the evolution of collaborative knowledge graphs, and
the interaction between Wikidata and emerging AI technologies.

The 6th Wikidata Workshop at ISWC 2026 welcomes contributions covering
the broad spectrum of research and applications related to Wikidata and
collaborative knowledge graphs. We are particularly interested in recent
developments in the Wikidata ecosystem, including new infrastructures
and capabilities such as GraphQL-based query access, Wikidata
partitioning and dataset extraction for large-scale experiments, and
embedding-based representations that enable semantic search, machine
learning, and downstream AI applications.

We also encourage work exploring the role of Wikidata in the rapidly
evolving Generative AI ecosystem, including AI agents, tool and skill
integration, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces,
retrieval-augmented generation, and knowledge grounding. These
directions highlight how collaborative knowledge graphs can provide
reliable, structured context for intelligent systems.

The workshop brings together researchers and practitioners from academia
and industry to share ideas, present innovations, and discuss the future
of open knowledge and AI-ready knowledge graphs.

events.title: 21st International Workshop on Ontology Matching (OM-2026)
events.organizers: Ernesto Jiménez-Ruiz, Sven Hertling, Huanyu Li, Cassia Trojahn, Oktie Hassanzadeh, Pavel Shvaiko and Jérôme Euzenat
events.description: Ontology matching is a key interoperability enabler for the Semantic Web, as well as a useful technique in some classical data integration tasks dealing with the semantic heterogeneity problem. It takes ontologies as input and determines as output an alignment, that is, a set of correspondences between the semantically related entities of those ontologies. These correspondences can be used for various tasks, such as ontology merging, data interlinking, query answering or navigation over knowledge graphs. Thus, matching ontologies enables the knowledge and data expressed with the matched ontologies to interoperate. The workshop has the following goals: 1) To bring together leaders from academia, industry and user institutions to assess how academic advances are addressing real-world requirements. The workshop will strive to improve academic awareness of industrial and final user needs, and therefore, direct research towards those needs. Simultaneously, the workshop will serve to inform industry and user representatives about existing research efforts that may meet their requirements. The workshop will also investigate how the ontology matching technology is going to evolve, especially with respect to data interlinking, process matching, web table and knowledge graph matching tasks. 2) To conduct an extensive and rigorous evaluation of ontology matching and instance matching approaches through the OAEI (Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative) 2026 campaign and 3) To examine similarities and differences from other, old, new and emerging, techniques and usages, such as process matching, web table matching or knowledge embeddings.

events.title: 6th International Workshop on Semantic Web and Ontology Design for Cultural Heritage, SWODCH 2026
events.organizers: Luca Biccheri, Antonis Bikakis, Roberta Ferrario, Béatrice Markhoff, Alessandro Mosca and Marianna Nicolosi-Asmundo
events.description:
SWODCH 2026 is the sixth edition of the International Workshop on Semantic Web and Ontology Design for Cultural Heritage. The purpose of SWODCH is twofold.

First, it aims to gather original research on foundational issues arising from the design of conceptual models, ontologies, and Semantic Web (SW) technologies for Cultural Heritage (CH) and the Digital Humanities (DH). The heterogeneous and multi-format data available in these domains call for principled methodologies and technologies to semantically characterise, integrate, and reason over data, as well as to support its retrieval, management, analysis, and visualisation. The workshop also welcomes studies addressing the philosophical and social analysis of CH and DH data and knowledge representation models, as ontologies in these domains often need to account for the historical and social dimensions of data.

Second, SWODCH aims to bring together stakeholders – scholars from Computer Science and the Humanities and GLAM professionals, representatives from CH institutions, etc. – who are involved in the development and deployment of concrete SW solutions for Cultural Heritage. This includes solutions for building, managing, exploring, visualising, or mining concrete or virtual knowledge graphs. In this context, SW solutions should be designed in accordance with the FAIR principles and support the creation of CH datasets and applications that adhere to these standards.

events.title: 3rd International Workshop on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Enabled by Knowledge Graphs (RAGE-KG 2026)
events.organizers: Daniel Dobriy, Marco Antonio Stranisci, Arianna Graciotti, Blerina Spahiu and Sahar Vahdati
events.description: RAGE-KG explores the state of the art and goes beyond in integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Knowledge Graphs as well as the synergies between Large Language Models and the Linked Open Data ecosystem. We aim to foster innovative RAG architectures relying on Semantic Web standards and new approaches to make Linked Open Data usable by LLMs, enhancing their ability to generate reliable, verifiable and context-aware responses based on structured, decentralized and authoritative data sources. This year the workshop welcomes a special track on RAG-systems for Human-AI Value Alignment, seeking contribution on RAG-based approaches for content moderation and harm reduction and to deal with human subjectivity. The workshop will be a full-day event featuring keynotes, paper presentations, and lightning talks on emerging RAG trends (e.g., agentic RAG), along with a dedicated session on the evaluation of RAG technologies aimed at building a community of practice on this theme.

events.title: 6th International Workshop on Scientific Knowledge Representation, Discovery, and Assessment (Sci-K 2026)
events.organizers: Allard Oelen, Anna Jacyszyn, Andrea Mannocci, Francesco Osborne, Georg Rehm, Angelo Salatino, Sonja Schimmler and Lise Stork
events.description: Recently, we have experienced a massive increase in the volume of scientific articles and research artefacts (e.g., datasets, models, software packages). This trend is expected to continue and opens up challenges including the development of large-scale machine-readable representations of scientific knowledge, making scholarly data and knowledge discoverable and accessible, and designing reliable and comprehensive metrics to assess scientific impact. Sci-K provides a forum for researchers and practitioners from different disciplines to present, educate, and guide research related to scientific knowledge. Three themes cover the most important challenges in this field: representation, discoverability, and assessment.

events.title: 17th Workshop on Ontology Design and Patterns (WOP)~2026
events.organizers: Abhilekha Dalal, Farhad Ameri, Christian Kindermann, Gunjan Singh, Alice Augustine and María Poveda-Villalón
events.description:
The Workshop on Ontology Design and Patterns (WOP) is an established venue for discussing best practices, reusable solutions, and methodological advances in ontology engineering. Now in its 17th edition, WOP continues to bring together researchers and practitioners interested in improving the quality, usability, and maintainability of ontologies through the use of design patterns and structured modeling approaches.

Ontology Design Patterns (ODPs) capture reusable modeling solutions to recurring ontology engineering problems. They support ontology developers by providing guidance on modeling decisions, facilitating reuse, improving interoperability, and enabling more systematic knowledge representation. Over the years, WOP has served as a forum for presenting new patterns, methodologies for pattern discovery and application, tools supporting pattern-based ontology engineering, and empirical evaluations of their effectiveness.

WOP 2026 aims to foster discussion around emerging challenges and opportunities in pattern-based ontology development, including applications in knowledge graphs, semantic technologies, and AI-driven knowledge engineering. The workshop encourages contributions from both theoretical and applied perspectives, as well as insights from real-world deployments. Through presentations and community exchange, WOP 2026 will continue to advance the role of ontology design patterns in high-quality knowledge engineering.

events.title: WikiKGQA: Wiki-Based Knowledge Graph Question Answering Challenge
events.organizers: Shakeeb Arzoo, Debayan Banerjee, Philipp Cimiano, Aidan Hogan, Alberto Moya Loustaunau, David Maria Schmidt and Ricardo Usbeck
events.description: KGQA has a long tradition in the Semantic Web community, particularly under the Question Answering over Linked Data (QALD) moniker and challenge series. With the rise of LLMs, the performance of state-of-the-art systems has improved dramatically. However, benchmark datasets in the space exhibit well-known limitations due, for example, to the manual cost of creating parallel corpora of natural language questions and structured queries. To address this issue, QAWiki (https://qawiki.org) proposes a collaboratively-edited community resource of hand-crafted question-query pairs, focusing currently on English & Spanish questions answered over Wikidata's SPARQL query service. The motivation is two-fold: (1) to evaluate KGQA systems over a hand-crafted collection of multilingual question-query pairs over Wikidata, and (2) to build a community centered around QAWiki, to expand and improve it, and thus expand and improve the resources available for training and benchmarking of KGQA systems.

events.title: 2nd International Workshop on Data Management for Knowledge Graphs (DMKG 2026)
events.organizers: Ruben Taelman, Olaf Hartig and Katja Hose
events.description:
The rapid increase in the adoption of knowledge graphs over the past years, both in the open data domain as well as the industry, means that data management solutions for knowledge graphs today have to support ever increasing amounts of data.

The continously growing KGs resulting from the increasing popularity of semantic technologies highlight the necessity for scalable and efficient solutions for management of knowledge graphs in distributed, federated, and centralized environments.

The DMKG workshop therefore invites novel research and advances in scalable data management solutions for large-scale knowledge graphs. Such data management solutions include techniques for storage and indexing, partitioning for decentralized/centralized systems, archiving and versioning, validation with SHACL/shEx, or federated data management. We welcome a broad range of papers including full research papers, vision papers, negative results, and system demonstrations.

The main goal of the workshop is to bring together both early-stage and established researchers as well as industrial partners in order to facilitate communication and collaboration between partners in different domains on the issues relating to scalable data management techniques for large-scale knowledge graphs.

events.title: KG-NeSy: The Third Workshop on Knowledge Graphs and Neurosymbolic AI
events.organizers: Shqiponja Ahmetaj, Fajar J. Ekaputra, Sebastian Neumaier, Andreas Ekelhart and Cogan Shimizu
events.description:
The Knowledge Graphs and Neurosymbolic AI Systems (KG-NeSy) workshop aims to bring together researchers and practitioners who are actively working on combining KGs and Neurosymbolic AI, exploring how these two research areas can mutually enhance one another. In particular, the workshop addresses the following complementary strands of research:

(1) KGs within Neurosymbolic (NeSy) AI systems, either as (a) deeply integrated components supporting hybrid reasoning, as (b) auxiliary structures improving explainability, interpretability, robustness, generalization, and transferability of deep learning models, or as (c) structured inputs enabling neurosymbolic prediction and inference.

(2) NeSy AI to support KG engineering. Neurosymbolic AI approaches can assist in the Knowledge Graphs engineering lifecycle, e.g., ontology construction, entity and relation extraction, knowledge integration and mapping, completion via logical reasoning or validation, refinement via learning-based methods, and continuous evaluation and maintenance. Even when KGs are not explicitly embedded inside Neurosymbolic AI approaches, these approaches can improve methods and tools for knowledge engineering, paving the way for the next generation of Knowledge Graphs development practices.

(3) KG-based approaches for understanding and systematizing NeSy AI, e.g., through design patterns, taxonomies, conceptual frameworks, or boxology representations. These works are crucial for identifying gaps in current approaches, aligning fragmented research landscapes, and opening up new opportunities for future developments.

events.title: SeMatS 2026 Third International Workshop on Semantic Materials Science: Harnessing the Power of Semantic Web Technologies in Materials Science
events.organizers: Andre Valdestilhas, Huanyu Li, Patrick Lambrix and Harald Sack
events.description: Technological solutions are essential for effectively using data in research, but compatibility issues in scientific data can impede progress. Interoperability and data access are key, making the Semantic Web a valuable solution. The link between Semantic Web (SW) technologies and Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) goes back to before 2001, with the Plinius ontology from 1994 as a significant example. Recent conferences such as FEMS-Euromat and the MSE Congress show increasing interest in SW applications. Additionally, the EU has proposed a Materials Commons for better access to materials science data. This workshop aims to highlight the use of SW technologies in MSE and make them more accessible. We will provide an overview of existing approaches, connect stakeholders, and promote collaboration. By leveraging SW technologies in MSE, we aim to enhance research outcomes and foster a more connected research environment.

events.title: Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Trustworthy Web Data Management
events.organizers: Gianluca Bonifazi, Stefano Cirillo, Eliana Pastor and Luca Virgili
events.description:
The rapid adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in data management and Web applications has created new opportunities for natural language access, reasoning, and decision support. However, concerns about reliability, hallucinations, bias, and lack of explainability limit their use in sensitive scenarios. Graph-based representations, such as knowledge graphs and property graphs, offer a promising approach to address these limitations by providing structured knowledge that can validate and explain LLM outputs.

The Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Trustworthy Web Data Management (GLOW) workshop explores how graph and Semantic Web technologies can enhance the trustworthiness of LLM-driven data management systems. In particular, it investigates graph-based retrieval and reasoning, ontology-guided modeling, and constraints that support more transparent and accountable LLM-based Web applications.

Now in its second edition, GLOW provides a dedicated space for research at the intersection of Semantic Web, Knowledge Graphs, and LLM-driven data-centric AI. The workshop builds on the success of its first edition, which attracted more than 20 submissions and resulted in a high-quality technical program.

events.organizers: Pasquale Lisena, Maria Angela Pellegrino, Lisa-Yao Gan, Yihang Zhao and Yiwen Xing
events.description: In an era where data shapes public discourse, Data-driven Storytelling: Bridging Semantics, AI, and Narrative (DDS 2026) aims to explore innovative methods for transforming complex datasets into engaging, interpretable narratives. This workshop focuses on the intersection of semantic technologies, artificial intelligence, and narrative design, seeking to make data more relevant, interactive, and shareable. We invite researchers and practitioners from diverse fields—including NLP, knowledge representation, HCI, Information retrieval and creative industries—to discuss frameworks and tools that enhance data engagement through storytelling, games, and art. Key topics include ontological coherence, generative AI, and participatory content creation, with the goal of empowering experts to communicate effectively in domains like education, journalism, and cultural heritage.

events.title: LLMs4OL 2026: Large Language Models for Ontology Learning
events.organizers: Hamed Babaei Giglou, Jennifer D'Souza and Sören Auer
events.description: As knowledge grows faster than ever, transforming unstructured text into structured, machine-understandable knowledge remains a central challenge in AI. This challenge explores the next frontier of Ontology Learning (OL)—moving beyond isolated subtasks toward fully integrated, intelligent systems. Building upon LLMs4OL tasks paradigms,  participants will tackle three visionary scenarios: building ontologies end-to-end from raw text, continuously extending existing knowledge structures, and learning taxonomies that generalize across domains. Together, these tasks reflect real-world demands where knowledge is dynamic, interconnected, and domain-spanning. Powered by the OntoLearner framework (https://ontolearner.readthedocs.io/), the challenge provides a unified environment for reproducible benchmarking, modular pipelines, and scalable evaluation. It invites researchers to push the limits of large language models in constructing, evolving, and transferring structured knowledge.

events.title: AIAA4KE: 1st Workshop on AI-assisted Approaches to Knowledge Engineering
events.organizers: Maribel Acosta, Heiko Paulheim, Evgeny Kharlamov, Diego Rincon-Yanez, Felix Sasaki, and Patrik Schneider
events.description:
The AI Assistants for Knowledge Engineering (AIAA4KE) 2026 workshop explores the potential of generative AI and agentic workflows in Knowledge Engineering. While AI-assisted approaches have revolutionised general software engineering, knowledge engineering — including ontology modelling and knowledge graph (KG) construction — remains a bottleneck, reliant on scarce human expertise.

AIAA4KE provides a platform to discuss topics such as multi-modal user intent analysis, automated ontology matching, and KG curation from diverse data sources. Key focus areas include developing evaluation benchmarks, integrating emerging standards like MCP-based agentic systems, and implementing human-in-the-loop governance for auditing AI-driven changes. We welcome presentations across the RDF/OWL and labelled property graph communities, aiming to scale knowledge engineering through robust, industry-ready AI assistants.

AIAA4KE seeks to connect three key communities:
• Research communities at the intersection of AI assistants and Semantic Web technologies focus on developing technically sound methods, but often lack opportunities to validate their work in real-world settings.
• Industry practitioners are actively building AI assistants for ontology and KG creation, yet face challenges around the accessibility of Semantic Web technologies and the difficulty of evaluating the quality and alignment of generated outputs.
• Standardisation experts, active in both academia and industry, are well-positioned to bridge these communities but are often underrepresented in the conversation.

By bringing these groups together, AIAA4KE aims to foster collaboration, accelerate innovation, and ensure that the combination of these technologies is both scientifically rigorous and practically applicable.

events.title: International Workshop on Structures to Stories: Multilingual NLP for Semantic Structured Data (IWSS)
events.organizers: Virginia Ramón Ferrer, Lia Draetta, Michael Oliverio, Rossana Damiano and Carlos Badenes-Olmedo
events.description:
Despite recent advances in LLM-based pipelines, the core multilingual Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Natural Language Generation (NLG) challenges of mapping between structured data and natural language, especially in low-resource and long-tail settings, remain largely unsolved and under-represented within the Semantic Web community.

The International Workshop on Structures to Stories: Multilingual NLP for Semantic Structured Data (IWSS) brings together researchers and practitioners advancing multilingual methods to (i) extract structured representations from text and (ii) generate faithful answers, verbalisations, explanations, and narratives grounded in structured evidence.

IWSS emphasises robust extraction, data-grounded generation, and realistic multilingual evaluation, with particular interest in under-represented languages, long-tail entities, and culturally specific concepts.

We invite full and short papers, position and negative-result papers, datasets, system demos, and resource papers. Topics include faithful multilingual verbalisation and summarisation, entity extraction and linking, schema/ontology alignment, and low-resource benchmarks and evaluation, among others.

events.title:
SPARK 2026 - First International Workshop on Spatial Intelligence and
Reasoning Enabled by Knowledge Graphs and Foundation Models
events.organizers: Amin Anjomshoaa, Manolis Koubarakis and Hamid Rabiei
events.description: Spatial intelligence plays a central role in understanding, modeling, and reasoning about complex real-world phenomena that are inherently geographic and spatiotemporal. With the growing availability of geodata and spatiotemporal data from sensors, Earth observation systems, digital twins, and location-aware services, there is an increasing need for methods that can effectively integrate spatial aspects into knowledge-based systems. This workshop aims to bring together researchers and practitioners working on spatial intelligence, geospatial data management, and spatiotemporal reasoning, with a particular focus on their integration within Semantic Web, Knowledge Graph and Foundation Model ecosystems.

events.title: ELMKE 2026: The 4th Workshop on Evaluation of Language Models in Knowledge Engineering
events.organizers: Reham Alharbi, Anna Sofia Lippolis, Bohui Zhang and Yuan He
events.description: The 4th Workshop on Evaluation of Language Models in Knowledge Engineering (ELMKE), co-located with ISWC 2026, focuses on advancing how language models (LMs) are assessed within knowledge engineering (KE). As LMs increasingly support tasks such as knowledge extraction, completion, and generation, robust and standardised evaluation remains a key challenge. Current approaches are often fragmented, heavily reliant on human judgement, and lack reproducibility, making it difficult to compare methods or build on prior work. ELMKE addresses this gap by fostering a community-driven effort to develop consistent, transparent, and scalable evaluation practices. The workshop brings together researchers and practitioners to share innovative methods, discuss limitations of existing approaches, and explore new paradigms for evaluating LM outputs. Particular attention is given to issues such as transparency, the role of human evaluation, and the broader implications of evaluation choices. In its fourth edition, ELMKE will feature presentations of recent research alongside interactive discussions aimed at shaping future directions. It also aims to encourage collaboration through the development of shared platforms, benchmarks, and dashboards, supporting long-term progress in reliable and reproducible evaluation for knowledge engineering.

events.title: Fourth International Workshop on Semantic Industrial Information Modelling (SemIIM)
events.organizers: Jieying Chen, Eduard Kamburjan, Baifan Zhou and Arild Waaler
events.description:
SemIIM 2026 focuses on advanced semantic information modelling, encompassing both foundational methods and large-scale industrial applications across data-intensive domains. With the rapid rise of digital twins and AI-driven operations, semantic modelling has become a critical enabler for structured, interoperable, and trustworthy data infrastructures. Across sectors such as manufacturing, energy, and high-tech systems, semantic technologies are increasingly deployed to support intelligent services, automation, and cross-system integration.

The workshop aims to bridge academia and industry by bringing together researchers, practitioners, and technology leaders. It provides a platform for presenting theoretical advances, modelling methodologies, engineering tools, and industrial case studies demonstrating how semantic technologies generate measurable operational value and contribute to emerging data and interoperability standards.

The program will feature invited keynotes and peer-reviewed contributions addressing the modelling of concepts, relationships, constraints, and operational rules for scalable data semantics. By connecting cutting-edge research with real-world deployments, SemIIM 2026 fosters dialogue on how semantic modelling can enable robust, explainable, and sustainable AI systems in complex industrial ecosystems.

events.title: International Workshop on Explainable AI and Knowledge Graphs (XAI+KG)
events.organizers: Roberto Barile, Roberto Confalonieri, Claudia D'Amato and Ernesto Jimenez-Ruiz
events.description: In recent years, the synergy between eXplainable AI (XAI) and Knowledge Graphs (KGs) has gained momentum as an essential approach for achieving trust and improving understanding in AI systems.  KGs provide structured and interconnected representations of (domain-specific) knowledge, XAI aims to provide insight for predicted results and/or to clarify how numeric machine/deep learning models function internally. By leveraging KGs within XAI, research can enhance the understanding and interpretability of AI models, making it easier for users to trust AI predictions. KGs can offer insights into the relationships and logic that AI systems use to reach conclusions. This can be particularly valuable in fields requiring high levels of transparency, such as healthcare, finance, and law, where understanding the rationale behind AI predictions and actions is crucial. Conversely, XAI can assist in constructing and refining KGs, helping to identify which aspects of KGs contribute most to accurate, reliable suggestions/conclusions. This workshop aims to bring together researchers, practitioners, and industry experts to explore challenges and opportunities of combining XAI with KGs, discussing novel methodologies, applications, and case studies. Contributions will span theoretical advances, practical tools, and industry applications.

events.title: Workshop on Knowledge Graphs and  Model-driven Systems Engineering (KGMDSE)
events.organizers: Robert Andrei Buchmann, Dimitris Karagiannis and Dimitris Plexousakis
events.description: This is a cross-over event aiming to stimulate the convergence between the communities focusing on Knowledge Graphs and those working on Model-driven Engineering of Information Systems. The initiative is motivated, among other factors, by the emerging notion of "Context Graphs" highlighting the importance of traceable decision-making and process knowledge, something that has been traditionally captured through enterprise modeling languages and execution traces associated with the enterprise aspects described through such languages. The recent uptake of the Agentic AI paradigm, with renewed interest in workflow orchestration and contextualized delegation, further suggests a growing relevance of this convergence. The workshop aims to stimulate a two-way exchange of knowledge and technical enablers - how approaches commonly employed in Model-driven Engineering can support KG-based systems or processes; and vice versa, how enterprise modeling methods and diagrammatic model contents can be augmented by KGs and KG-based AI systems. Furthermore, we also look at KG-LLMs integration patterns that can benefit from model-driven engineering practices, towards novel knowledge-driven architectures and knowledge conversion modes.

events.title: Personal Knowledge Graphs for LLM-Powered Decentralized Recommendations
events.organizers: Oshani Seneviratne and Fernando Spadea
events.description: Personalized recommendation systems increasingly influence how users discover information, products, services, and opportunities. However, contemporary recommendation approaches often rely on centralized user profiling and opaque machine learning pipelines that limit transparency, user agency, and privacy. Personal Knowledge Graphs (PKGs) provide a Semantic Web-native approach to representing user preferences, behaviors, context, and provenance, enabling recommendation systems that are explainable, interoperable, and user-centric. Recent advances in KG retrieval, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), federated learning (FL), and large language models (LLMs) have further expanded the possibilities of PKG-driven personalization. This tutorial introduces participants to the emerging area of PKG-powered recommendation systems. Participants will learn how PKGs can serve as semantic foundations for personalization, how decentralized learning architectures preserve user data sovereignty, how KG retrieval can support explainable recommendations, and how LLM-based recommendation systems can be grounded using personal and external KGs. The tutorial combines conceptual presentations with extensive hands-on activities using open-source notebooks, datasets, and software. Participants will construct PKGs, build recommendation pipelines, perform KG retrieval, and explore approaches for mitigating over-personalization and filter bubbles.
